# All Core Devs - Execution (ACDE) #208, March 27, 2025

* [March 27, 2025, 14:00-15:30 UTC](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/converter.html?iso=20250327T140000&p1=1440&p2=37&p3=136&p4=237&p5=923&p6=204&p7=671&p8=16&p9=41&p10=107&p11=28)
    * 🕐 **DST warning: double check your local time** 🕐 
* 90 minutes
* Stream: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0eVoE_isGBk

# Agenda 

- Pectra 
    - Hoodi 
        - Fork activation
        - Application/infra testing
    - https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/1409
    -  [eth_config JSON-RPC Method](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7910)
    - [Mainnet timing](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1374#issuecomment-2741823829)
- Fusaka 
    -  PSA: [`PFI` deadline past](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-7607-fusaka-meta-eip/18439), client team preferences due by March 31, scope freeze on April 10  
        -  PFI PRs:
            - https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9528
            - https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9451 
    - PeerDAS 
        - Sunnyside labs update
        - EL Cell Proof computation   
    - EOF next steps. 
       - Pre-reads:
          -  https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/eof_fusaka_options 
          - https://hackmd.io/@pcaversaccio/eof-when-complexity-outweighs-necessity
          - https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1374#issuecomment-2749792454
      - Positions shared: 
          - Geth: 
            - [EOF alternative](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9501)
            - [Option D: "Introspecting EOF" support](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1374#issuecomment-2755988812)
          - Besu: [support, unsure about options A, C, or (least favored) D](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1374#issuecomment-2757961705)
          - Erigon: [EOF support, option unspecified](https://erigon.tech/a-lean-approach-to-fusaka-our-stance-on-a-minimal-fork/)
          - Nethermind (Mar. 4): [EOF support, incl. TXCREATE](https://x.com/m25marek/status/1896911082628727213)
          - Reth (Feb 19): [EOF support, options unspecified](https://www.paradigm.xyz/2025/02/what-comes-after-ethereums-pectra-hard-fork) 
          - Vitalik: [support Introspecting EOF or no-EOF, but specific EVM changes](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1374#issuecomment-2755164606)
          - Solidity:  [support EOF, option unspecified](https://soliditylang.org/blog/2025/03/27/the-case-for-eof/) 
    - Fusaka scope:
        - Besu, Erigon, Nethermind, Reth preferences shared (Geth messing) 
        - [EIP-7883:  ModExp Gas Cost Increase](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7883) unanimously favored
- Portal & History Expiry
     - [EIP-6110 interactions](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1374#issuecomment-2741993183)
     - eth/69 
     - Deployment timelines
     - [Light client <> Portal issues](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1399#issuecomment-2755435584) 
- [Protocol Research Call](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/protocol-research-call/23261) 
- [Sepolia replacement name](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/testnet-name-needed-for-sepolia-replacement/23221) 


Facilitator email: tim@ethereum.org

>    * The only relevant testnet is Sepolia, and everyone agreed to test on Sepolia.

### Bikeshedding
Testnet name needed for Sepolia replacement. Only mention if there is time.
https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/testnet-name-needed-for-sepolia-replacement/23221
I want to propose this EIP for Fusaka as a partial replacement for EOF: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9501

Ipsilon would like to discuss planning options for EOF based on this document: https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/eof_fusaka_options - which proposes the existing plan and a few other plans removing the introspection bans to varying degrees.
I'de like to share the `eth_config` EIP as well https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7910 (preferably earlier in the agenda than EOF)
I want to discuss the PAY opcode in relation to EOF.
I would like to discuss a proposal to formalize the Ethereum Protocol Upgrade Process: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/1409 (comments on PR ahead of call would be very welcome)

ether.fi has planned the testing for Pectra features and is about to dive into active testing soon. The mainnet schedule around the end of May should be fine for us to catch up. However, since ether.fi's withdrawal credential contracts are controlled by EigenLayer, we need to coordinate with them on this aspect.

One clarifying question I have is whether it will be possible to combine validators with different withdrawal credentials. As far as I know, the spec no longer explicitly restricts this scenario due to the introduction of [[EL-triggered consolidations](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3775/files/143b9e623dce1f134b33ec70c892ac2f8eae87c8#top)], but I'd like confirmation if this is indeed supported on the execution side.

Regarding EOF-or-alternatives, I feel like we can think about the available options as a ladder:

1. Do nothing at all
2. No EOF, but do keyhole solutions to solve a the top 2-3 problems asked for by EOF supporters, perhaps:
    * Increase code size limit to 128kB
    * Add a DUP/SWAP opcode that takes a 1-byte immediate argument, or alternatively just add 32 more for each one to increase the max depth to 48
    * Code sections (though this one could be delayed until we do 7701, which is the only use case for it that I know for now
3. Do EOF, but greatly simplified by removing some of its most challenging goals, eg. no gas or code observability
4. Do EOF, roughly as planned

I personally think (2) and (3) are both reasonable!

> do keyhole solutions

[Simple keyhole solution](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9548) for the codesize DoS
IMHO Code size increase should be done in all 4 options, regardless of what is chosen.

If time permits, I'd like to briefly share about some devnet testing work Sunnyside Labs has been doing for PeerDAS. (previous reports  [1](https://testinprod.notion.site/Sunnyside-Devnet-Updates-03-11-Internal-1b38fc57f54680a9a409d639a8a45bdd?pvs=74), [2](https://testinprod.notion.site/Sunnyside-Devnet-Updates-03-18-Internal-1b98fc57f54680d991c3f7a4fefa590b), [3](https://testinprod.notion.site/Sunnyside-Devnet-Updates-03-25-Internal-1c08fc57f54680339b2fe2dbc8232b6d)). 

We're working with the CL teams in running devnet tests with PeerDAS to quantify how much blobs we can raise over the current limit and identify any bottlenecks as we're getting there. We'd like to give a quick heads up and ask for some help from EL team as well if we observe any issues with the EL when handling high blob counts.

For code sections, it would be useful for EVMifying the precompiles: One section could contain the gas function and the default section the actual calculation. That expresses the precompile in EVM code as well as retaining the same gas profile (for precompiles where this is valuable, so not modexp).  This is something that I've backburnered while getting EOF out the door, so there are more uses for code sections than EIP-7701 and subroutines.  

There are also ways to leverage it to get the cleanly observable effect of "pseudo-opcodes" like my SCREDIT/SDEBIT EIP-7519 as well as the SRETURN/MRETURN/TRETURN proposal (EIP-7877) that have positive impacts in things such as proving that a storage interation was "+100" by code intent, improving concurrency analysis.

@seongyun-ko 

you can indeed consolidate a _source_ validator into a _target_ validator, assuming:
1) source has an execution withdrawal credential type
2) source withdrawal credential address matches the `msg.sender` that called the EIP-7251 contract
3) target has a compounding withdrawal credential type

as long as the request is authenticated (i.e. `msg.sender` matches the source validator withdrawal credential address) the request can specify any target validator to receive the source validator's balance

the only restriction on the target validator is condition (3)

feel free to test consolidations first on the `hoodi` testnet, or refer to the specs to verify any of the above

@ralexstokes 

> you can indeed consolidate a source validator into a target validator,

This is extremely interesting and something we didn't pick up when the EL change went in. From a safety perspective, it is perfectly fine for us, as everything goes through EL. From a roadmap perspective, it opens up some opportunities. Thank you for confirming.

>  **Client teams, please share your thoughts in advance.**

Thoughts on EOF. Irrespective of details, I think it is important to evolve the EVM, and I firmly believe that a fundamental change to the EVM has to:

- (1) be done all at once, in one step, rather than incrementally
- (2) have a backwards-compatibility path
- (3) be on Ethereum mainnet first, and then percolate out towards other systems using EVM

(1) EOF exists as the result of years of EVM improvement proposals, all integrated into a single change. It is not a simple, but combines a lot of smaller improvements into one, while decreasing the amount of functionality available to contracts. That latter point is an important one. The EVM was designed before any contracts existed. Ten years later, the pain points are pretty well known. There is a workaround for (almost) everything, but I feel it's important to take a step to remove the unnecessary stuff. In order to make it less painful for tooling authors and contract authors, it is good not to drag out this change. EOF is a clean-room redesign and needs to go in as such.

(2) Obviously, the question of legacy contracts always comes up. While EOF removes some EVM features, it is also strictly additional for Ethereum since it's a new mode of execution on top of legacy EVM, which remains in the system indefinitely. I have two points on this:

- It wouldn't be Ethereum if we didn't have backwards-compatibility. For every upgrade touching the EVM so far, the core devs have meticulously analyzed all existing contracts to ensure no important ones get broken (with some notable exceptions, such as GasToken). Some changes are just not possible without breaking contracts, so this is why EOF must be introduced as a 'second option'
- With the introduction of EOF, the legacy mode will not receive new functionality anymore. The interpreter will effectively remain frozen, the only possible upgrade being gas cost tweaks. For implementers, this means EOF will most likely be implemented as a separate EVM, and all new development will focus there.

(3) In my opinion, the best place to fundamentally change the EVM is Ethereum itself. If an L2 project launched with a new and radically different EVM, it wouldn't be compatible with Ethereum, and it's not worth doing. Introducing a large change on Ethereum first is the only way to ship this improvement.

### Implementation

As team lead of Geth, I state that I prefer **option D) Introspecting EOF** from [Ipsilon's document](https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/eof_fusaka_options) for Fusaka. However, I would also like to note that Geth is internally divided on this issue, with some people on the team strongly arguing against including EOF at all. They can, and will, speak for themselves on the call.

I recommend option D because 

- it contains all the important EVM changes
- it requires the least changes to the existing EOF implementation in Geth
- it does not remove gas introspection and code introspection. I strongly believe both introspection features are needed, and removing them is weird and requires a lot of workarounds in the spec. AFAIK, it was originally proposed to remove code introspection in order to make it possible to upgrade contracts transparently. While this would be neat if it worked, I feel the drawbacks of removing code introspection make it not worth it. For gas introspection, it introduces similar problems, where some EVM usage patterns become impossible, requiring strange workarounds in EOF.

I made a few ordering changes to the agenda: 

* @shemnon @fredriksvantes I think both of your topics should be addressed before talking about Pectra mainnet timelines
* @mininny scheduled your update, if there's anything you can share ahead of the call, that'd be ideal
* @pipermerriam @KolbyML @fjl @ralexstokes I bundled all the Portal/history expiry topics for the end of the call. We can re-prioritize on the fly when we know how much time, if any, we have to discuss this after everything else 😄 !

> (2) Obviously, the question of legacy contracts always comes up. While EOF removes some EVM features, it is also strictly additional for Ethereum since it's a new mode of execution on top of legacy EVM, which remains in the system indefinitely. I have two points on this:
> 
> * It wouldn't be Ethereum if we didn't have backwards-compatibility. For every upgrade touching the EVM so far, the core devs have meticulously analyzed all existing contracts to ensure no important ones get broken (with some notable exceptions, such as GasToken). Some changes are just not possible without breaking contracts, so this is why EOF must be introduced as a 'second option'

Regarding legacy->EOF conversions; EOF is only validated at contract deployment, so some constraints could be relaxed for on-chain contract conversions of existing contracts.

EOF doesn't change the meaning of any exiting opcodes, so should be ok doing that (i.e. "grandfathering" in the use of those opcodes)

Code introspection would however be more problematic (also the code would be inherently different); but worst case could be got around by sidecar ing prior code for data contract type things 🤔 Would need some analysis/reserach around this

### Fusaka scope client team perspectives

Currently have Besu, Erigon, Nethermind, Reth.  Plus Base L2.
https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-7607-fusaka-meta-eip/18439/3

I spoke with Etan and I no longer think what I said makes sense to try and do. The problems I am encountering and the solution space has already been explored going back to 2022, so I think if we were to try and do anything to do with SSZ on the EL side for "Serialization Harmonization", it should be through Etan's Meta [EIP-7919](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7919), basically fully committing to it.

The Lido protocol successfully passed the hardfork activation on Hoodi

Before the hardfork, we had the complete core protocol running, with external node operators ([~14 active rn](https://operators-hoodi.testnet.fi/operators)) and one external oracle. Four staking modules have been connected to the protocol, including [Simple DVT](https://operators-hoodi.testnet.fi/module/2) (with Obol and SSV clusters running) and the [Community Staking Module](http://csm.testnet.fi/) (which allows anyone to permissionlessly run a validator as part of Lido on Hoodi).

Most of the core UIs have been deployed, such as widgets for [stakers](https://stake-hoodi.testnet.fi/), and for [community](http://csm.testnet.fi/) and [curated](https://operators-hoodi.testnet.fi/) operators. Monitoring infrastructure for the protocol and validators has been deployed. The Lido Ecosystem Grants Organization ([LEGO](https://lido.fi/lego)) has also provided a grant to Protofire, who have already deployed a [Hoodi Safe](https://app.safe.protofire.io/) for everyone on Hoodi to use (similar to the Holesky Safe launched with a grant from Lido).

Before the hardfork, the Lido on Hoodi protocol was upgraded as per [LIP-27](https://github.com/lidofinance/lido-improvement-proposals/blob/develop/LIPS/lip-27.md) to ensure compatibility with Pectra. _Please note that protocol upgrade solely concerns compatibility to maintain nominal operation, rather than integrating new functionality introduced in the Pectra hardfork._

The protocol passed the Pectra hardfork without any major issues. The protocol and validator states were tested in accordance with the introduced changes. No issues were detected within the Lido protocol or among external participants, apart from the issues noted concerning Erigon and Lighthouse which affected some Node Operators and nodes used for infrastructure and off-chain tooling.

If possible, I'd like to present EIP-7819 that was one the schedule 2 weeks ago.

Note: Just like the PAY opcode, this is Mega EOF related
Solidity's position on EOF: https://soliditylang.org/blog/2025/03/27/the-case-for-eof/

The Besu team is still very much in favour of EOF, but is split between options A and C. The disagreement revolves around banning code introspection. Part of the team thinks it requires too big changes in the current workflow of sc devs and it is questionable if forced code conversion should be even done in the first place. Option D is almost equal as C, but not banning code introspection and still banning CREATE and CREATE2 does not make much sense. We prefer Option C because of that.
The other part of the team prefers option A because it is the most future-proof approach for the EVM and unlocks more flexibility for any possible changes to the EVM.

> Solidity: [support EOF, option unspecified](https://soliditylang.org/blog/2025/03/27/the-case-for-eof/)

We're in favor of option A, complete EOF.

But none of the options is a deal-breaker to us and any of them is better than no EOF at all.

> Increase code size limit to 128kB

I proposed https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7903 and https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7907 in the last two weeks which address the codesize limit. JUMPDEST analysis is not the only problem here - especially for loading code, there are several other O(n) vectors which require costing the load on a per-byte or per-word basis.
I've also drafted an EIP to fix EVM memory pricing, at https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9556. (There is definitely room for some tweaking, especially around memory limits).

If possible, id like to propose a change to transaction receipt post-pectra
